rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the form as declinable because it has come onto a singular pattern, like علانية and كراهية.
rows.anchor: قاله الزجاج , وصرف لصيرورته على وزن المفرد نحو علانية وكراهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gold bracelets are presented as a sign that Pharaoh's claim is true, like adornments given to a servant sent on an important mission.
rows.anchor: والسوار : ما يوضع في العصم من الحلية { من ذهب } ليكون ذلك أمارة على صدق صحة دعواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh demands angels accompany Moses in such numbers that they fill the space and stand close, as advocates who can secure his request.
rows.anchor: { الملائكة } أي هذا النوع , وأشار إلى كثرتهم بما بين من الحال بقوله : { مقترنين }

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Pharaoh's boast in controlling the waters is answered by his drowning in them: whoever exalts himself through something besides God may be destroyed by it.
rows.anchor: به - أفاده القشيري . ولما كان كلامه

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Pharaoh belittled Moses for poverty and low status, but God empowered Moses over him; the lesson is that one who belittles another may be overcome by him.
rows.anchor: إلا غلبه - أفاده القشيري .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though thoughtful hearers would see Pharaoh's speech as self-degrading, his followers accepted it because worldly leadership commands the weakly attached, while people resist an unrecognized leader despite great deeds.
rows.anchor: فهم أذل شيء لمن ثبتت له رئاسته دنيوية وإن صار ترابا , وأعصى شيء على من لم تفقه له الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh used deceptive, beguiling speech that diminished his own case to sway people already disposed to foolishness.
rows.anchor: أي بسبب هذه الخدع التي سحرهم بها في هذا الكلام الذي هو في الحقيقة محقر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their obedience meant acknowledging Pharaoh's kingship and grandeur, affirming his lordship, and rejecting Moses' command.
rows.anchor: بأن أقروا بملكه وأذعنوا لضخامته واعترفوا بربوبيته وردوا أمر موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses had answered every threat and request with signs that surpassed bracelets and angels, so the Egyptians had no reason to obey Pharaoh except affinity in evil character.
rows.anchor: أجابهم إليه , فلم يكن للقبط داع إلى طاعة فرعون بعدما رأوا من الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Egyptians had forceful resolve and pride, except when confronted with the worldly means they were accustomed to obey.
rows.anchor: { قوما } أي عندهم قوة شكائم توجب لهم الشماخة إلا عند من يقهرهم بما يألفون من أسباب الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their فسق was entrenched departure from God's obedience into disobedience, made a second nature.
rows.anchor: عريقين في الخروج عن طاعة الله إلى معصية , قد صار لهم ذلك خلقا ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means they repeatedly provoked intense divine anger by angering God's allies, as in the cited hadith qudsi, “I was sick and you did not visit Me.”
rows.anchor: بإغضاب أوليائنا كما في الحديث القدسي ( مرضت فلم تعدني ) لنكثرهم مرة بعد مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God requited them with terrible punishment and drowned every one of them; none escaped despite their number and strength, an extraordinary destruction requiring great exertion.
rows.anchor: أوقعنا بهم على وجه المكافأة لما فعلوا برسولنا عليه السلام عقوبة عظيمة منكرة مكروهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their destruction made them predecessors and examples for those who incur divine anger, seek earthly domination, and meet destruction in this life, the next, or both.
rows.anchor: سلفا } متقدما لكل من يهلك بعدهم إهلاك غضب في الهلاك في الدنيا والعذاب في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author concludes from the cited verse that Pharaoh certainly belongs among the people of the Fire.
rows.anchor: المنتج من غير شك أن فرعون من أصحاب النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's seizure of Pharaoh and his troops and casting them into the sea is cited as the fate of wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: فأخذناه وجنوده فنبذناهم في اليم فانظر كيف كانت عاقبة الظالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh and his followers are cited as leaders who call to the Fire, receive no help at Judgment, and are cursed and disgraced.
rows.anchor: وجعلناهم أئمة يدعون إلى النار ويوم القيامة لا ينصرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier peoples named with Pharaoh all denied the messengers, so the divine punishment applied to them as well.
rows.anchor: كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح وعاد وفرعون ذو الأوتاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The familiar image of boiling water powerfully warns or repels, even though the reality being compared may exceed it.
rows.anchor: لما كان للتذكير بما يعرف شأن عظيم من الإقبال أو التنفير وإن كان دون ما شبه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الحميم is water whose heat has reached its extreme through the fire burning beneath it, seeming to struggle to escape the heat.
rows.anchor: الماء الذي تناهى حره بما يوقد تحته , فهو يثبت كأنه يريد أن يتخلص مما هو فيه من الحر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet saying that one drop of zaqqum would ruin earthly livelihoods; the food of someone fed it in Hell is far worse. Al-Tirmidhi calls it hasan sahih; al-Hakim says it is sahih on both authorities' conditions, and al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, and Ibn Hibban also transmit it.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( لو أن قطرة من الزقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to seize him forcibly, leaving him no control over his own affairs.
rows.anchor: أخذ قهر فلا تدعوه يملك من أمره شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They drag him by force, with roughness, violence, and speed, toward torment and humiliation, as though he were being carried.
rows.anchor: بغلظة وعنف وسرعة إلى العذاب والإهانة بحيث يكون كأنه محمول

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi defines عتل as gripping the gathered front of a person's garment at the chest and dragging him.
rows.anchor: وقال الرازي في اللوامع : والعتل أن يأخذ بمجامع ثوبه عند صدره يجره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading with ḍamma conveys greater severity and roughness than the reading with kasra.
rows.anchor: وقراءة الضم أدل على تناهي الغلظة والشدة من قراءة الكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سواء means the middle; الجحيم is the fiercely blazing Fire and the place from which the tree that feeds him emerges.
rows.anchor: { إلى سواء } أي وسط { الجحيم } أي النار التي في غاية الاضطرام والتوقد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boiling punishment is poured over his head from every direction so that it surrounds his whole body.
rows.anchor: { فوق رأسه } ليكون المصبوب محيطا بجميع جسمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean punishment produced by boiling water or the boiling water itself; calling it punishment makes the threat more terrifying.
rows.anchor: العذاب الذي يغلي به الحميم أو الذي هو الحميم نفسه , والتعبير عنه بالعذاب أهول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their former blessing of rain from heaven is answered by boiling heat on the outside and zaqqum within.
rows.anchor: في مقابلة ما كان لهم من البركة بما ينزل من السماء من المطر ليجتمع لهم حر الظاهر بالحميم والباطن بالزقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The taunting command recalls the messengers' worldly warning that the sinner was lowly, which he and his followers denied; repeating their boast adds rebuke and torment.
rows.anchor: حكى له قولهم على ما كانوا يلفظون به زيادة في تذعيبه بالتوبيخ والتقريع معللا للأمر بالذوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أنت is emphatic and isolates him as the one supposedly mighty, in contrast to those who truthfully exposed his worthlessness.
rows.anchor: وأكد بقوله : { أنت } وحدك دون هؤلاء الذين يخبرون بحقارتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: العزيز means one who overcomes and is never overcome; الكريم combines generosity with dignity of soul and proud refusal.
rows.anchor: العزيز } أي الذي يغلب ولا يغلب { الكريم } أي الجامع إلى الجود شرف النفس وعظم الإباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent praise is an ironic accusation of baseness, established by the sinner's present ruin rather than concealed by pretended high character.
rows.anchor: فهو كناية عن مخاطبته بالخسة مع إقامة الدليل على ذلك بما هو فيه من المهالك

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i reads إن with fatḥ, making the punishment both spoken and enacted in the same way the sinner was praised in worldly life and believed himself deserving of praise.
rows.anchor: وقراءة الكسائي بفتح ( إن ) دالة على هذا العذاب قولا وفعلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This refers to the punishment in words, deed, and lived condition, confirming what the deniers used to doubt.
rows.anchor: { إن هذا } أي العذاب قولا وفعلا وحالا { ما كنتم } أي جبلة وطبعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They labored to force themselves into doubt and away from their original disposition to affirm what is possible, especially for a proven truthful messenger with miracles.
rows.anchor: تعالجون أنفسكم وتحملونها على الشك فيه وتردونها عما لها من الفطرة الأولى من التصديق بالممكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After singling out one sinner as an example among the Prophet's community, the passage generalizes the blame to those sharing his sins, then turns to their opposite, the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: وأفرده أولا إشارة إلى قليل في قوم هذا النبي الكرمي الذي تداركهم الله بدعوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God-fearing dwell in a settled place from which they do not want to move and where they are safe from everything unpleasant.
rows.anchor: { في مقام } أي موضع إقامة لا يريد الحال فيه تحولا عنه { أمين } أي يأمن صاحبه فيه من كل ما لا يعجبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gardens and springs are beyond the mind's ability to describe and delight the eyes.
rows.anchor: { في جنات } أي بساتين تقصر العقول عن إدراك وصفها كل وصفها { وعيون } كذلك بحيث تقر بها العيون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sundus is fine silk made for outer garments; istabraq is thick silk used for linings and named for its strong sheen.
rows.anchor: { من سندس } وهو ما رق من الحرير يعمل وجوها , وزاد صنفا آخر فقال : { وإستبرق } وهو ما غلظ منه يعمل بطائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They face one another physically and in affection; none turns away, and curtains screen them when they desire their women.
rows.anchor: { متقابلين } أي ليس منهم أحد يدابر الآخر لا حسا ولا معنى , وود أن كلا منهم يقابل الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording confirms that the astonishing description is true exactly as stated.
rows.anchor: قال مؤكدا له : { كذلك } أي الأمر كما ذكرنا سواء لا مرية فيه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: زوجناهم means pairing them as spouses, not contracting marriage: marriage contracts serve to make relations permissible, whereas Paradise is beyond legal obligations of permission and prohibition.
rows.anchor: { وزوجناهم } أي قرناهم كما تقرن الأزواج , وليس المراد به العقد لأنه فعل متعد بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companions are allocated white, beautiful maidens with pure clothing; عين describes their wide eyes.
rows.anchor: بجواري بيض حسان نقيات الثياب { عين } أي واسعات الأعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some listen with great effort hoping to find a flaw in the recitation with which to sow doubt among the weak.
rows.anchor: { ومنهم من يستمع } أي بغاية جهده لعله يجد في المتلو مطعنا يشك به على الضعفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular listener follows the grammar of من and signals the few who listen; the shift to plural follows its meaning and signals the many who turn away or mock.
rows.anchor: ولما أفرد المستمع نظرا إلى لفظ ( من ) إشارةإلى قلة المستمع جمع نظرا إلى معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both the hostile listeners and others who heard the sermon ask the question after leaving, doing so in blindness, feigned ignorance, and mockery.
rows.anchor: { إذا خرجوا } أي المستمعون والسامعون جميعا { من عندك قالوا } أي الفريقان عمى وتعاميا واستهزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive wording magnifies beneficial knowledge; God prepared its recipients with clear minds free of ego and responsive to primordial nature.
rows.anchor: { للذين أوتوا العلم } أي بسبب تهيئة الله لهم بما آتاهم من صفاء الأفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آنفا means just now, shortly before they left; its sense is linked to the first or foremost part, as with the beginning of prayer.
rows.anchor: { آنفا } أي قبل افتراقنا وخروجنا عنه من ساعة - أي أول وقت - تقرب منه

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan construes آنفا as a circumstantial accusative meaning beginning or newly initiated, asking what the Prophet had just begun to say before they separated.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : حال , اي مبتدئا , أي ما القول الذي ائتنفه الآن قبل انفصالنا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects treating آنفا as an adverb: the explanation gives its sense, and he knows no grammarian who classifies it as an adverb.
rows.anchor: ورد كونه ظرفا بأنه تفسير معنى , وأنه لا يعلم أحدا من النحاة عده في الظروف

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi says ائتنفت الأمر means I began the matter, while أنف الشيء is its beginning.
rows.anchor: وقال البغوي : ائتنفت الأمر : ابتدأته , وأنف الشيء أوله

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil's account says the Prophet preached and censured hypocrites, who mockingly asked Ibn Masud what Muhammad had said as they left the mosque.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : وذلك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يخطب ويعيب المنافقين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says that he was among those who were asked.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : وقد سئلت فيمن سئل .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sealed their hearts so that they neither believed nor understood for benefit; such rigid indifference results from that seal.
rows.anchor: فلم يؤمنوا ولم يفهموا فهم الانتفاع لأن مثل هذا الجمود لا يكون إلا بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By following their desires they abandoned reason and human restraint, neglected the greatest discourse, and pursued worldly accumulation; they are the people of Hell described before the Garden parable.
rows.anchor: أي مجانبين لوازع العقل وناهي المروءة , فلذلك هم يتهاونون بأعظم الكلام ويقبلون على جمع الحطام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guided strive through listening to follow primordial nature, attain guidance through sincere faith and surrender, and undertake varied spiritual exertions.
rows.anchor: اجتهدوا باستماعهم منك في مطاوعة داعي الفطرة الأولى إلى الوقوع على الهدى بالصدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God increases their guidance by opening and illuminating their hearts with the lights of spiritual witnessing, making them vessels of wisdom.
rows.anchor: بأن شرح صدورهم ونورها بأنوار المشاهدات فصارت أوعية للحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links the increase of guidance to the verse saying that the Lord guides believers who do good by their faith.
rows.anchor: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات يهديهم ربهم بإيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God shows them what to fear and enables them to avoid it despite desire; they are the first group described as standing on clear proof from their Lord.
rows.anchor: بين لهم ما هو أهل لأن يحذر ووفقهم لاجتنابه مخالفة للهوى , فهم القسم الأول

rows.speaker: ابن برجان
rows.claim: Ibn Barjan says piety is the action of faith, just as the limbs' deeds are the action of Islam.
rows.anchor: قال ابن برجان : التقوى عمل الإيمان كما أن أعمال الجوارح عمل الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra guides to noble manners by honoring the Prophet in relation to himself and his community; outward reverence is evidence of inward faith, just as faith in God requires outward deeds performed with their conditions, pillars, and limits.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الإرشاد إلى مكارم الأخلاق بتوقير النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالأدب معه في نفسه وفي أمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra's central aim is careful observance of manners with the Prophet; it opens al-Mufassal, a summary of the Qur'an, as al-Fatiha's opening aim is vigilance toward God.
rows.anchor: فحاصل مقصودها مراقبة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الأدب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second section of al-Mufassal begins with a disconnected letter, just as the second of the remaining Qur'an divisions begins with such letters.
rows.anchor: وابتدئ ثاني المفصل بحرف منن الحروف المقطعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name al-Hujurat clearly signals the sūra's purpose through the verse bearing that name.
rows.anchor: واسمها الحجرات واضح الدلالة على ذلك بما دلت عليه آيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala's names describe God as majestic, who rejects deeds from those who slight His Messenger; merciful in establishing etiquette for salvation and in guiding the discerning toward reward.
rows.anchor: { بسم الله } الملك الجبار المتكبر الذي من أخل بتعظيم رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يرض عنه عملا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage follows religious brotherhood and bans conduct prompted by self-admiration over ancestry; it overturns lineage-based privilege and directs believers to piety.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر سبحانه الأخوة الدينية تذكيرا بالعاطف الموجب للإكرام , المانع من الانتقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address includes everyone, believers and others alike.
rows.anchor: أي كافة المؤمن وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings were created from nothing in their varied forms and lineages, from a male described as the locus of resolve and strength and a female as a place of weakness and repose; neither confers superiority.
rows.anchor: { من ذكر } هو المقصود بالعزم والقوة { وأنثى } هي موضع العضف والراحة , لا مزية لأحد منكم في ذلك على آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Peoples branch from a common origin; tribes lie beneath them, followed by subgroups, clans, branches, and families in a six-level lineage hierarchy.
rows.anchor: جمع شعب بالفتح وهو الطيبقة الأولى من الطبقات الست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He illustrates the lineage levels as Khuzayma (people), Kinana (tribe), Quraysh (subtribe), Qusayy (clan), Abd Manaf (branch), Hashim (family), and al-Abbas (household).
rows.anchor: خزيمة شعب , وكنانة قبيلة , وقريش عمارة , وقصي بطن

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi says no lineage group after the عشيرة is given a recognized collective name.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : وليس بعد العشيرة حي يوصف به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse names only peoples and tribes because these are the furthest lineage divisions people can readily recognize; the divisions below them are clearer still.
rows.anchor: واقتصر على الأولين لأنهما أقصى ما يسهل على الآدمي معرفته فما دونه أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lineage divisions let people identify relatives and fulfill kinship duties, not recite pedigrees or boast.
rows.anchor: أي ليعرف الإنسان من يقاربه في النسب ليصل من رحمه ما يحق له , لا لتواصفوا وتفاخروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prior verse's religious kinship implies that people should fear God in their relatives and those tied to them by family.
rows.anchor: كان التقدير : فتتقوا الله في أقاربكم وذوي أرحامكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against those who assume honor comes from lineage, the verse makes the most God-fearing the noblest before God, who alone grants honor and perfection.
rows.anchor: مبطلا للتفاخر بالأنساب معللا لما أرشد إلى تقديره السياق مؤكدا لأجل ما عندهم من أن الكرم إنما هو بالنسب

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says the best of people in the pre-Islamic era are the best in Islam when they gain understanding; the author explains this as a habit of understanding that leads to action.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( خياركم في الجاهلية خياركم في الإسلام إذا فقهوا )

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the true jurist is one who acts on his knowledge.
rows.anchor: كما قال الحسن رحمه الله : إنما الفقيه العامل بعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier deniers knew the resurrection claim was true but denied it in a rush of desire, without considering the outcome, falling into habitual error.
rows.anchor: صح أنهم يعلمون ذلك ولم يحملهم على التصريح بالتكذيب به إلا المبادرة إلى ذلك بغلبة الهوى من غير تأمل لعاقبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the context rejects resurrection and a warner from their own people brought it, God consoles the Prophet: a shared affliction is easier to bear, and the Qur'an's majestic verses confirm its warning and admonition.
rows.anchor: كان السياق لإنكار البعث الذي جاء به منذر من القوم المنذرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine ending on كذبت signals the deniers' low status beside God's majesty.
rows.anchor: وسم الفعل بالتاء إشارة إلى هوانهم في جنب هذا المجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition is omitted before قبلهم because the powerful, numerous earlier groups seemed to occupy their whole age and land.
rows.anchor: أسقط الجار فقال : { قبلهم } . ولما لم تكن لهم شهرة يعرفون بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's people are not identified by a further lineage name; their own messenger faced overwhelming numbers and strength and endured their harm for nearly ten centuries.
rows.anchor: { قوم نوح } وأشار إلى عظيم التسلية بأنهم جاءهم منذر منهم , وكانوا في القوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waters of sky and earth converged and drowned Noah's people, a striking display of God's power and freely chosen action.
rows.anchor: التقى عليهم الماءان : ماء السماءن وطلع إليهم ماء الأرض فأغرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the Well were swallowed when the well and its surroundings collapsed, taking them and their possessions; their story is told in al-Furqan.
rows.anchor: أي البئر التي تقوضت بهم فخسفت مع ما حولها فذهبت بهم وبكل ما لهم كما ذكرت قصتهم في الفرقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamud's sign is evidence for resurrection and their destruction parallels the earlier groups; unlike the people of the Well, they were not swallowed by the earth, but a quake followed a blast carried by the wind.
rows.anchor: ولما اتفق قوم هود عليه السلام والقبط بالإهلاك بالريح التي أثرت بها صيحة ثمود , أولئك مع الحجارة والرمل
